name: Romosozumab
route_note: subcutaneous injection 210 mg (two 105 mg injections) once monthly for 12 months, then an antiresorptive

discovery.note: Developed after rare high-bone-mass disorders (sclerosteosis, van Buchem disease) were traced to loss of sclerostin (SOST gene, 2001).

tagline: An antibody against sclerostin that builds bone and curbs resorption at once
summary: Romosozumab is a humanised monoclonal antibody against sclerostin, a natural brake on bone formation. A year of monthly injections both increases bone formation and decreases resorption, rapidly raising bone density and reducing fractures, but it carries a boxed warning for heart attack and stroke.
mechanism: Sclerostin, secreted by osteocytes, binds LRP5/6 co-receptors and inhibits canonical Wnt signalling in osteoblasts. Blocking it with romosozumab activates Wnt signalling, increasing osteoblast activity and bone formation.

Romosozumab also reduces RANKL expression and so decreases bone resorption — a 'dual effect' distinct from teriparatide. The anabolic effect wanes after about a year, so treatment is limited to 12 months followed by an antiresorptive drug.
uses: Osteoporosis in postmenopausal women at high risk of fracture
Osteoporosis in men at high fracture risk (Japan, EU and some other regions)

history.title: Sclerostin gene identified
history.detail: Loss-of-function SOST mutations are shown to cause sclerosteosis, a disorder of very high bone mass.

history.title: FRAME
history.detail: FRAME shows romosozumab reduces new vertebral fractures by 73% versus placebo at 12 months.

history.title: ARCH
history.detail: ARCH shows romosozumab followed by alendronate outperforms alendronate alone but finds more serious cardiovascular events.

history.title: Approvals
history.detail: Evenity is approved in Japan (January), the US (April, with a boxed warning) and the EU (December).

history.title: Guideline adoption
history.detail: The Endocrine Society's 2020 guideline update recommends romosozumab for postmenopausal women at very high fracture risk.

pk.metabolism: catabolism to peptides and amino acids

safety.boxed_warning: Potential risk of myocardial infarction, stroke and cardiovascular death; do not start in patients with MI or stroke within the past year.

facts: The drug target was discovered by studying families with sclerosteosis in South Africa and van Buchem disease in the Netherlands.
Romosozumab treatment is limited to 12 monthly doses.

references.title: Saag KG et al. ARCH trial (NEJM 2017)
